a.label: Connections issued

b.label: Refills actually taken

framing: A gas connection is a precondition for clean cooking; a refill is the cooking. The scheme was justified on the second and is reported on the first.
gapReason: Different quantities — cumulative connections against refills per beneficiary per year. No subtraction is meaningful.

a.label: Households with a tap

b.label: Households receiving water to standard

framing: Certification records a tap installed, not water delivered — a distinction the Ministry's own functionality assessment made.
gapReason: Different denominators. 82% is of ALL rural households; 76% is of CERTIFIED households, a subset of connected ones. Neither bounds the other, so no national functional-coverage figure is derivable and '6 points' would be invented.

a.label: Cards created

b.label: Hospital admissions authorised

framing: A card confers eligibility. An admission is care received. The two are cited interchangeably and differ by an order of magnitude.
gapReason: An eligibility stock against a flow of cumulative events. Subtracting them would compare a population to a count of episodes.

a.label: Houses sanctioned

b.label: Houses completed

framing: The only pair in the dataset where both sides share a unit, so the wedge is real — and the chain does not end here.
notes: 0.92 crore. Occupancy, the third stage, has no measurement — see the absence declared on pmay-g-completed.

a.label: Headline network figure

b.label: The build record

framing: Not a usage pair. The second is the honest measure of the same activity the first overstates: roughly 54,004 km of the network increase is reclassified state roads.
gapReason: Different quantities — network length in kilometres against build rate in kilometres per day. The relation is correction, not conversion.

a.label: Facility count

b.label: Routes actually operating

framing: Airports were counted on a broadened basis including heliports and waterdromes; roughly half the routes launched to serve them have since stopped.
gapReason: Facilities against routes — different objects entirely.

a.label: Track commissioned

b.label: Ridership against projection — no published series

framing: Metro projects were approved on ridership forecasts and a 14% return threshold; whether they meet those forecasts is not published as a series.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist. Evidence comes from one-off CAG audits and academic studies, so the track figure cannot be qualified by anything and must not be read as though it had been.

a.label: Households connected

b.label: Hours of supply received — no national series

framing: Saubhagya connected 2.86 crore households in eighteen months. How many hours a day they receive power is not measured nationally.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist. Survey evidence indicates around 53% of villages received under twelve hours a day, but there is no continuous series.

a.label: Net payroll additions

b.label: First-time entrants — no measurement exists

framing: Net additions include re-joiners and job-switchers, so the same worker can be counted repeatedly; India maintains no register that would separate them.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist. No establishment-level longitudinal payroll register exists, so first-time entry cannot be extracted from the net figure.

a.label: Workers registered

b.label: Benefits delivered — not published

framing: e-Shram exists because the 2020 exodus showed the state could not identify its informal workforce. Whether registration converts into delivered social security is not reported.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist as a series. Registration is published; downstream disbursement keyed to those identifiers is not.

a.label: Population with basic sanitation

b.label: What independent survey found

framing: Rural India was declared open-defecation free in October 2019; independent panel evidence from the four states that mattered most found 44% still defecating in the open.
gapReason: Different populations and different instruments — a national WDI series against a four-state panel survey. The counterpart is a dispute between sources, not a series.

a.label: PLFS, official

b.label: CMIE, private

framing: The two instruments disagree about the direction of employment change, not merely its level — over 2017-18 to 2021-22 they record growth of opposite sign.
gapReason: Two figures that disagree about the sign of a change have a disagreement, not a gap. Neither is the corrective; neither may be shown alone.

a.label: PLFS, official

b.label: CMIE, private

framing: Roughly twenty percentage points apart, with the divergence concentrated almost entirely among women and showing no convergence across reference periods.
gapReason: A disagreement between instruments, not a measurable wedge.

title: PMLA cases initiated versus persons convicted

a.label: Cases initiated

b.label: Persons convicted

framing: The canonical coverage-versus-outcome pair for this domain. Reporting cases initiated without convictions, or the completed-trial conviction rate without the count of cases still pending, produces a materially different picture in either direction. Neither series may be rendered alone.
gapReason: Cases initiated and persons convicted are different quantities on different denominators (P-52); the two do not subtract.

title: Shutdown orders issued versus shutdown orders published

a.label: Shutdown orders issued

b.label: Shutdown orders published

framing: An absence-pair: the coverage side is a third-party reconstruction and the usage side does not exist because the orders were not published, despite a binding direction to publish. The pair exists so the missing half renders as a finding rather than as an empty chart.
gapReason: The usage side does not exist: the orders were not published despite a binding direction to publish, so there is nothing to place beside the reconstructed count.

title: RTI applications filed versus information actually received

a.label: RTI applications filed

b.label: Information actually received

framing: Application volume is the coverage measure routinely cited; the usage measure is the share of applicants who obtained the information sought. Assessment work has found well under half succeeding, with under a tenth of the unsuccessful filing appeals, but the underlying assessment has not been pulled as a primary document and neither series is yet authored. Declared here so the pair is visible as owed rather than silently absent.
gapReason: The counterpart is not authored yet, so nothing is placed beside the coverage figure and no difference is stated.

title: What Grade 3 children can do: the household test against the official survey

a.label: Children who read a Standard II text, tested one-on-one at home

b.label: Children rated proficient in language, on a written paper at school

framing: The domain's central measurement question, side by side. Both are headcount ratios of Grade 3 children, which is why they can be shown together at all - and they answer 27.1 per cent against 57. Neither may be rendered alone.
gapReason: Different populations and different instruments. The household test covers every child resident in a sampled rural household, enrolled or not, present or not, and is administered orally one-on-one; the official survey covers children enrolled in a sampled school and present on test day, replaces absentees, includes urban India, and is a four-option written paper with a 25 per cent guessing floor. Subtracting them would state a difference between two quantities that no linking study, equating design or anchor item connects - and the proficiency band's cut-scores are published nowhere, so the second number's definition is not available to check.
notes: The honest reconciliation is not subtraction but thresholding, and it is a comparison of an earlier vintage than the two series shown above. Applied to NAS 2017's own Grade 5 data, a World Bank Minimum Proficiency Level benchmark puts 54 per cent below it, against ASER 2018's 49.5 per cent of Standard V unable to read a Standard II text. Five points apart, same direction, same population, same years - and neither figure may be carried forward to 2024, since NAS 2017 breaks comparison with everything after it and the 2024 Standard V reading is 48.8, that is 51.2 per cent unable. Most of the headline contradiction is a category error between a mean and a headcount; what survives it is that the official survey's state rankings correlate with nothing.

title: How long India's schools were shut: two measures, opposite answers

a.label: Weeks schools were fully closed

b.label: Weeks schools were not fully open, UNESCO's own definition

framing: On one measure India ranks 58th of 210 countries and looks unremarkable; on the other it is the unique global maximum. Both come from the same dataset and the same custodian, and a claim in either direction that does not name its measure is unusable.
gapReason: The two are nested rather than opposed - full closure is a subset of the days the headline measure counts - so the arithmetic difference is simply the partially-open days, and stating it as a gap would imply the two are rival estimates of one quantity when they are two definitions of closure. The residual is also uninterpretable on its own: India spent 476 days in a single 'partially open' bucket covering everything from one grade in one state shut to all primary grades shut nationally, and no state-wise or grade-wise series exists.
notes: The reconciliation is grade-differentiation: for most of the partially-open days senior grades had reopened while primary had not, which is what makes India's national number look mild and its primary-grade reality severe. Primary is where the learning loss landed.

title: The national pupil-teacher ratio against the schools that meet the norm

a.label: The national average, published every year

b.label: Schools meeting the norm, school by school - not published since 2015-16

framing: RTE section 25 imposes the staffing duty 'in each school'. The state publishes a national mean against it and discontinued the distributional measure that would answer it, although it holds school-level enrolment and teacher counts for every school in the country.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist for any year after 2015-16, so there is nothing to subtract. A mean and a compliance share are also different quantities: an average of 20:1 is consistent with any distribution, including one in which about a lakh schools have a single teacher and a quarter of schools sit above 35:1.
notes: The discontinued series is authored separately and runs to its last published value: 25.93 per cent of primary schools above the norm in 2015-16, at which point the measurement stopped. The only computation since is a university centre's, from 2021-22 microdata, and it is not the government's.

title: Quota children reimbursed against quota seats filled

a.label: Children in schools for which reimbursement is claimed

b.label: Seats notified against seats filled - no national measure exists

framing: The entitlement in RTE section 12(1)(c) is a share of entry-class seats. The state reports a cumulative headcount of children being paid for and publishes no seats denominator, so the one quantity that would say whether the entitlement is being delivered has never existed as a national statistic.
gapReason: There is no denominator to subtract from. Worse, where the Ministry uses the word 'seats' the figure is a lagged reimbursement headcount - for one state it equals exactly the previous year's approved reimbursement count for three consecutive years, producing a hundred per cent fill rate by construction - so a fill rate computed from Ministry data would be an artefact rather than a measurement.
notes: The absence is not an impossibility. A DISE-based exercise measured seats against filled nationally for 2012-13 and 2013-14 - fill rates of 21.5 and 29.0 per cent on about 21.1 lakh seats - which establishes the quantity is constructible from data the school system already collects.

title: The vacancy rate that is reported against the vacancy statistic that is not maintained

a.label: The rate tabled when Parliament asks

b.label: A defined, maintained national vacancy statistic

framing: Two ad-hoc aggregates assembled on request, differing by 1.12 lakh posts for the same year, stand in for a statistic the Department told a parliamentary committee it does not maintain and declined to start maintaining.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist, so nothing is placed beside the reported rate. The two aggregates that do circulate cannot be differenced either: neither defines its levels or its school universe, so the 1.12 lakh difference between them cannot be attributed and the total is carried as a range or not at all.
notes: The rate's own denominator moves: sanctioned posts rose 10.4 per cent in one year, with secondary posts up 60.3 per cent, so the reported rate fell from 15.16 to 14.07 per cent while the absolute number of vacant posts rose by 23,514.

title: What India spends on education: the two official numerators

a.label: What education departments spend

b.label: What the government calls education spending

framing: The Ministry publishes both, side by side, in one table, for the same year - and across FY2013-14 to FY2021-22 one rises while the other falls. Rendering either alone states a direction for the last decade that the other reverses.
gapReason: A disagreement about what counts as education spending, not a gap between delivery and use. The difference is also not a constant that could be reported as one figure: it runs from 0.52 points of GDP in FY2004-05 to 1.46 in FY2016-17, roughly tripling, because the broad column additionally carries training and the education spending of about 44 other ministries whose share of the total rose from 15.9 to 33.3 per cent.
notes: Parliament is briefed on the broad number and the 6 per cent target is invoked against it, so the gap to target is 1.9 or 3.3 points depending on a choice that is never stated when the target is quoted. Both terminal points are Budget Estimates and the series stops at FY2021-22.

title: The school stock published against the school closures not published

a.label: Government schools standing, counted each year

b.label: Schools closed or merged each year

framing: The state publishes how many schools exist and declines to publish how many were shut, so the circulated 'schools closed' figure is a stock difference netting closures against openings.
gapReason: A stock difference is not a closure count: it nets openings against closures and says nothing about how many schools were merged rather than shut, or how many children were displaced. Subtracting two years of the stock would produce exactly the misleading number this pair exists to prevent.
notes: The absence is disputed rather than accepted: the Ministry's stated reason is that opening and closing are state functions, while it operates a school-level database with a unique code per school from which closures are directly derivable, and publishes flow-type counts for zero-enrolment and single-teacher schools over the same years.

title: Literacy as recorded against reading as demonstrated

a.label: People recorded as literate, on someone's word

b.label: Children who can actually read a Standard II text, tested

framing: Every official Indian literacy instrument asks and none tests: a literate person is a person someone said was literate. Placing the recorded figure beside an administered reading task is the only way the difference between the two is visible.
gapReason: Different populations, different constructs and different denominators - all persons aged 7 and above nationally against children enrolled in Standard V in rural households - so no subtraction is meaningful and the two must never share an axis. The pair exists to show the two side by side with that warning, not to state a difference.
notes: More than half of Standard V children cannot read a text pitched three grades below them - and every one of them, on reaching 15 with 'primary' recorded as attainment, is counted literate by the labour survey's ladder, by the modular survey's Class I rule, by the international recoding of both, and by the Census too if an informant says so. Where both methods were run on the same respondents the gap was 5.6 points, and that is a floor: the card test is one sentence with partial credit.

title: Higher education entered against higher education completed

a.label: Students enrolled

b.label: Students who complete - no national measure exists

framing: India added 1.08 crore higher-education students in a decade and has never published a dropout, retention or completion rate for any of them, so the entire expansion is measured only at entry.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist. The survey publishes a stock (enrolment) and an annual flow (out-turn) but never links a cohort from entry to exit, so subtracting them would compare an enrolled population to a year's graduating count across different cohorts and produce a number that means nothing.
notes: Established by exhaustive search rather than inferred: every report from 2014-15 to 2023-24 was searched for dropout, retention, completion rate and transition rate, with zero occurrences in every one. The school system's own data covers school education only, so nothing fills the gap from the other side.

title: Civilians killed in Kashmir: the ministry's count against the press-derived one

a.label: Civilians killed, as the Home Ministry counts them

b.label: Civilians killed, as a press-compiled register counts them

framing: For 2018 these read 55 against 86; for 2016 the press register reads 14 against the ministry's 15, and for 2020 and 2021 it reads below the ministry too. Two counts of one word that cross over, and neither may be shown alone.
gapReason: The two are not one quantity measured with error. The ministry's figure counts civilians killed in terrorist-initiated incidents and in counter-terrorism operations, merged, on returns booked and forwarded by police stations and the territorial administration, on a basis never defined in seventeen report years. The press register counts persons it classifies as civilians killed in incidents it classifies as terrorism-related, compiled from news reports, with no published definition of 'civilian', no methodology page of any kind, and a conceded but unspecified component of internally developed data. They gate on different things and fail in opposite directions - press reportability misses routine, remote-sector and blackout-period events, administrative reportability misses events the state has an interest in not booking - so neither is a superset of the other and subtracting them would state a difference between two quantities nothing connects.
notes: The crossover is the point. Ratios to the ministry's bounded series run 2.21 in 2018, 1.08 in 2019, 0.89 in 2020 and 0.88 in 2021 - above in one year, below in two - so the obvious hypothesis, that the press register simply catches the protest and encounter-site deaths the ministry omits, is contradicted by 2016, the year of the largest protest death toll in the period, in which the press register reads below the ministry. The two civilian series must not be treated as interchangeable in any year on the strength of their agreement in others. Neither publisher has ever acknowledged, compared or explained the gap on any reachable page.

title: How many incidents there were in 2018: 614, 417 or 228

a.label: Incidents, as the ministry published them at the time

b.label: Incidents militants initiated, as the ministry publishes them now

framing: One ministry has published three different numbers for the same object in the same year - 614, 417 and 228 for calendar 2018 - across two restatements neither of which carried a note, and every public comparison across that boundary compares unlike things.
gapReason: The difference between the two is not a residual with a meaning. Part of it is the un-merging of security-force operations from the composite, which is exactly quantified from 2018 by the encounters column; part of it is whatever the 2021-22 restatement removed, which is 197 events for 2018 and 339 for 2019 against no change at all in 2020, and which MHA has never described. The pre-restatement basis is unestablished and the obvious candidate is ruled out by MHA's own later reply, so a subtraction would be a number built on a basis nobody can state.
notes: The intermediate basis is carried separately as jk-terrorist-incidents-merged, which reads 417 for 2018 and is the sum of the two published components exactly, four years out of four. Two further counts exist for the same year from the press-derived register - 597 on its widest basis and 206 on its fatality-gated one - so five separately published, separately labelled incident counts exist for calendar 2018 alone. The near-coincidence of 228 and 206 is arithmetic accident: one gates on who initiated, the other on whether anyone died, and they must not be read as corroborating.

title: Operations the state counts, consequences it does not

a.label: Encounters and counter-terror operations conducted

b.label: What those operations produced - no term of any kind

framing: This is the only column in the ministry's entire J&K instrument that counts what the state did, and 731 operations over seven years sit beside no count of what they produced.
gapReason: The counterpart does not exist. There is no count of civilians killed in these operations separately from the merged column, no count of cordon-and-search operations, no count of magisterial inquiries ordered, completed or published, and no sanction figures in the same instrument. The J&K chapter of the Annual Report 2024-25 contains zero occurrences of 'human right', 'NHRC', 'custody', 'custodial', 'compensation', 'ex-gratia', 'inquiry' or 'magisterial' across roughly 46,000 characters, so there is nothing to subtract from and nothing to qualify the operations count with.
notes: The instrument also counts the outcomes of an activity it does not count. Cordon-and-search operations are the most common form of contact between the security forces and the civilian population and produce the detentions, the property damage and the encounters that are counted; the string 'cordon' appears zero times in seven Annual Reports, and two independent searches found no published CASO count from MHA, the J&K Police or the Army for any year. That absence is declared on the same series at index 0.

title: The pellet harm the state published against the pellet harm it refused

a.label: Deaths by pellets, published month by month

b.label: Injuries by pellets - specifically asked for, specifically refused

framing: One question asked for the injured and the killed. One answer supplied seventeen deaths across three calendar years and refused everything else in the interest of national security, and the order of those two facts is the argument.
gapReason: Not a gap but a refusal, and the two are different quantities in any case - deaths against injuries, not a subset relation that subtraction could express. Nor is there an agreed injury figure to subtract towards: the figures in circulation are at least five different objects on five different windows, counting persons, patients, eyes, admissions, referrals and payments, and no source states its unit.
notes: This pairing carries the phase's sharpest asymmetry: the only pellet quantity in the public record is the one that is smallest and most favourable to the weapon's defenders, and the quantities on which the criticism rests are the ones withheld. The same table also carries a second column - security-force personnel killed during law-and-order protests, two in July 2016 and nothing else - which makes it the only official Indian document located in this phase that places harm to civilians and harm to the state's own personnel on one page. It exists precisely to the extent that both terms are small, and it was never repeated.

title: Infiltration attempted against infiltration estimated to have succeeded

a.label: Attempts recorded

b.label: Persons the ministry estimates got through

framing: Two rows of one table, published side by side for a decade and quoted interchangeably: any claim that infiltration fell from 419 to 53 and any claim that it fell from 136 to 14 are quoting different rows.
gapReason: MHA publishes no interception or attrition figure that would link the two rows, so the difference between them is not a published or derivable quantity. One row is labelled an estimate and the other is not, and MHA nowhere states how an attempt is detected or counted - so subtracting a defined-basis-unknown count from an estimate would produce a number whose basis is unestablished twice over. The Ministry of Defence's 'Infiltration Bid Eliminated' cannot supply the missing term either: it is scoped to the Line of Control under Army operational control and is neither the same geography nor the same agency.
notes: Both series terminate at 2022 and the table was deleted from the Annual Reports 2023-24 and 2024-25 with no announcement, while the policy paragraph on containing infiltration survives. The three infiltration quantities move in opposite directions under one underlying reality - if interception improves, attempts may be unchanged, bids eliminated rise and net falls - so a gap in one must never be filled from another.

title: Local recruitment: three official answers for one year, and no return behind any of them

a.label: What officials have said the recruitment figures are

b.label: The published return that would settle them - none exists

framing: The quantity most often quoted in the argument about whether militancy in Kashmir is indigenous is the one quantity in this domain with no instrument at all, and its published claims contradict each other by 30 to 120 per cent for the same year.
gapReason: There is nothing to subtract on either side. One side is a set of press-conference claims which conflict with one another - 187, 218 and over 200 for 2018; 100, 110 and 130 for 2022; 10 and 22 for 2023 - and the other is the absence of any statistical return, in seventeen consecutive Annual Reports and in every parliamentary reply retrieved. No published definition of recruitment exists from any body, so even a single agreed figure would have no stated basis.
notes: An unusual application of the pair layer, recorded as such: neither side is a series, because no series exists. It is carried because the two sides genuinely may not be shown alone - a recruitment figure rendered without the absence beside it reads as a point on a series, and the absence rendered without the claims beside it loses the fact that the state asserts numbers it has never published. The pre-2018 figures of 66, 88 and 126 exist because an MLA asked and a Chief Minister answered in writing; that route terminated in 2018 and the restored assembly is barred from the subject matter, so the instrument changed from an answer to a claim.

title: Civilian deaths with a perpetrator named, against civilian deaths with none

a.label: All civilian deaths, no perpetrator named

b.label: Civilian deaths attributed to the armed forces - the only instrument that ever named one

framing: One instrument merges civilians killed by militants with civilians killed in the state's own operations and attributes neither; the other named the perpetrator for every death it could and left the largest bucket unattributed rather than forcing it. The second stopped publishing in 2020.
gapReason: The two are not rival estimates of one quantity and no arithmetic connects them. The official figure is a merged count on returns compiled by a party to the events and published without attribution; the non-official one is a perpetrator-split of a differently-bounded civilian universe, compiled from media monitoring, field verification and court-registry records with no formal inclusion criteria, whose 2019 total of at least 80 exceeds the official 44 for the same year. Subtraction would imply a subset relation that neither publisher asserts and that no definition supports.
notes: This pair is the answer to the ledger question for civilian deaths, and it is a negative one: two-sided accounting for this quantity existed, was non-official, and stopped. Its final figures are a floor stated as such by the body that produced them, which declared a complete information collapse in Kashmir after 5 August 2019. After 2019 no instrument of any provenance publishes the perpetrator split - not MHA, which has never had a column for it; not GTD, which covers non-state perpetrators only by construction; not UCDP, which records Government-of-India one-sided violence in three country-years ever and none after 2002. Kashmir Law and Justice Project is the only identified live candidate successor and was not investigated in this phase.

title: Detenus counted in J&K's own prisons, against detenus moved out of them

a.label: Detenus recorded in Jammu and Kashmir's prisons at 31 December

b.label: PSA detenus moved out of the territory, who leave that row and enter another State's

framing: The recorded stock falls from 404 in 2019 to 228 in 2020 across the largest detention wave in the territory's recent history, and in the same window 295 detenus were moved to prisons in other States, where the only instrument that counts them attributes them to the State that holds the body.
gapReason: One is a 31 December stock of all preventive-detention detenus, the other a within-year flow of PSA detenus specifically, so they are neither the same population nor the same kind of quantity and subtraction would produce nothing. Nor could the transferred detenus be added back: Prison Statistics India publishes an aggregate 'Belongs to other State' column that never names the origin State, has no interstate transfer table for detenus at all where it has one for convicts and one for undertrials, and the transfer series is a relayed count from a document nobody in this phase retrieved. The two sides are placed together so that the fall in the first is not read as a fall in detention.
notes: The direction of the order is the argument: a is what the state publishes about itself, b is the movement that removes people from it. The strongest evidence that b is real and not inferred comes from inside a - NCRB's own Table 2.12B records Uttar Pradesh holding zero out-of-State detenus at 31 December 2018 and 188 a year later, and Haryana holding 27 of whom none were Haryana-domiciled, matching to the unit a parliamentary answer that does not cite it. But PSI will not say those detenus came from J&K, and that attribution must be imported from outside PSI or not made at all.

title: Ten official detention figures for August 2019, and the year-wise series that would settle them

a.label: What the Ministry has stated the detention numbers are

b.label: The published year-wise PSA series that would settle them - none exists

framing: Ten figures on five undeclared objects were given to Parliament over sixteen months, and the one instrument that would let a reader tell which of them counts what has never been published by the body that necessarily holds it.
gapReason: There is nothing to subtract on either side. One side is a set of point figures on populations that are not the same population - preventive custody under section 107 CrPC, a preventive-detention stock, a PSA stock, PSA orders expressed per person, and an undefined category given twice with a fourteen-case discrepancy - and the other is the absence of any year-wise return at all. A gap between two of the figures is not a quantity: the difference between 451 and 396 is a real decomposition the Ministry itself stated on one date, and the difference between 7,357 and 396 is a difference of legal instrument, not a residual.
notes: Neither side is a series, because no series exists, and the pair is carried because the two sides may not be shown alone. A detention figure rendered without the absence beside it reads as a point on a series, and the absence rendered without the figures beside it loses the fact that the state has produced PSA-identified numbers on request more than once and never as a run. The producibility is not in doubt: every detention order carries a district-year serial number, so each District Magistrate necessarily knows how many were issued; the J&K Home Department produced a five-year year-wise series of the detenus it moved out of the territory on a single sheet; and the Ministry decomposed 451 into 396 PSA and 55 CrPC in a single sentence on 11 March 2020.

title: Two official J&K detenu counts whose difference is exactly the foreign-national count

a.label: NCRB's detenu row, from returns furnished by the J&K Prison Department

b.label: The 'Detained' prison category, from J&K prison records tabled in the Rajya Sabha

framing: Two official instruments count preventive-detention prisoners in Jammu and Kashmir, neither cites the other, and they differ in all six overlapping years - and in every year where both can be decomposed the difference is exactly the foreign-national count, which means the parliamentary series silently excludes foreigners and never says so.
gapReason: The differences across the six years are 28, 36, 37, 40, 30 and 48, and three of them are explained exactly rather than approximately: in 2014, 2015 and 2018 the parliamentary figure equals NCRB's count of J&K-domiciled detenus to the unit, with NCRB's 28, 36 and 30 foreign detenus accounting for the whole of each gap. For 2016 and 2017 the domicile decomposition was not retrieved, so the implied residuals of 37 and 40 are consistent with the same explanation and are not evidence for it. For 2019 the two figures are on different dates - a November figure against a 31 December one - so no residual could be computed even with the decomposition in hand. Subtraction across the whole series would therefore present an inference as an arithmetic result, and the one place it can be done it produces zero rather than a gap.
notes: The out-of-territory rows of the same two documents corroborate each other exactly - 27 J&K prisoners lodged in Haryana in the parliamentary answer, 27 out-of-State detenus and no others in Haryana's NCRB row for the same year - which is corroboration between two official sources rather than between a source and its own echo, and is the strongest single check in the detention subject. The Uttar Pradesh rows do not corroborate, at 234 against 188, because one counts all J&K prisoners to November and the other counts detenus only at 31 December. Those must not be reconciled: the difference is roughly the J&K convicts and undertrials in UP jails, which is a real quantity nobody has stated.

title: The undertaking to restore statehood, against the condition that would test it

a.label: What the Union and the Court have said about restoring statehood

b.label: The stated trigger condition - never defined by anyone, including the body that must satisfy it

framing: Six statements over seven years commit the Union to restoring statehood on conditions - the situation normalising, an appropriate time - that no document from any source has ever defined, so whether the commitment is due cannot be answered in either direction.
gapReason: One side is a set of undated commitments in four different formulations, and the other is the absence of any definition of the condition on which they turn. There is no quantity on either side and no arithmetic that connects them: a stated condition that admits no test cannot be subtracted from a stated commitment. The two judicial formulations are also not reconciled by any retrieved document - the majority states elections and restoration as independent obligations, Kaul J treats restoration as conditional on elections having been held, and elections have been held since October 2024.
notes: The pair is carried because the undertaking was load-bearing on something else: it is the statement 'in view of' which the Supreme Court declined to determine whether a State may lawfully be converted into a Union Territory at all. So the one question that would have tested the conversion was set aside on a commitment whose trigger has never been defined, and shown alone the commitment reads as a policy in progress rather than as the consideration for a declined adjudication.

title: The detenus the state moved out, against the number the holding prison refused to give

a.label: PSA detenus the J&K Home Department records moving out of the territory

b.label: The number of them in the prison that held them - asked for, and refused

framing: The territory that moved 1,122 detenus out can produce a year-wise count of them on one sheet, and the prison that received them refused under the Right to Information Act to disclose even how many it held.
gapReason: Not a gap but a refusal, and the two are different quantities in any case - a within-year flow of transfers out against a stock held in one named prison on a date. Nor is there an agreed figure to subtract towards: the transfer series is relayed from a document nobody retrieved, and the refused figure was never produced at all. The Public Information Officer declined the aggregate along with the identities, relying on a 2008 Uttar Pradesh circular and a third-party-information ground, so the smaller and less sensitive number was withheld with the larger one.
notes: The order of the two sides is the argument. Moving a detenu across the territorial boundary moved the Right to Information addressee with him, from a department in Srinagar with a relationship to his family, community, courts and press, to a prison administration in another State with none. The transfer power and the information refusal are the same fact seen twice, and this is the cleanest withheld in the phase precisely because the refusal is dated, addressed and attributed, and covered the bare number.

title: The suspension orders published after the judgment, against the ones refused before it

a.label: Suspension orders published by the J&K Home Department, from January 2020

b.label: The orders that imposed the August 2019 blackout - the Supreme Court asked for them and did not get them

framing: The series that measures compliance with the publication direction begins in the month the direction was given, and the orders it does not contain are the ones the Union claimed privilege over when the Court ordered their production three months earlier.
gapReason: There is nothing to subtract. One side is a count of orders in a numbered series that began in January 2020; the other is the complete absence of any 2019 order from that series or from any archive, and the reason it is absent is a refusal rather than a shortfall. Nor are the two sides the same object even in kind: the published series consists of confirmations of police directions, and what was asked for in October 2019 was the orders by which communication had been blocked. A difference between a count and a refusal is not a quantity.
notes: The order of the two sides is the argument and it runs in the government's favour on one half. The publication is real: the Department began posting numbered orders within days of the judgment, publication is written into the order's own distribution list alongside the press and the Gazette, and the mechanism can be shown to have existed in 2019 because unrelated Departmental orders carry the same website line throughout that year. That is what makes the 2019 zero a finding rather than a coverage gap. This pair is deliberately NOT a restatement of the all-India orders-issued-against-orders-published pair: for J&K the second side is no longer empty after January 2020, which is a different situation from the national one, and the two must not be conflated.

title: Three official numbers for how many suspension orders J&K has issued, and no Union count at all

a.label: What the published series, the UT and the police file numbers each say the order count is

b.label: A Union count of J&K suspensions - declined rather than unavailable

framing: Three incommensurable official numbers exist for orders in one territory, and the Union that holds the power in that territory keeps none of them, on the ground that police is a State subject in a place that is not a State.
gapReason: The three numbers on one side are on different windows and different definitions and cannot be netted against each other, let alone against the other side. The derived series count covers calendar years on partial archive coverage; the UT's 93 runs from the judgment to an undated closing date and mixes at least two kinds of order; and the Authorized Officers' file references are not counts of anything at all. The other side is not a smaller number but the absence of any number: both Union bodies have said they hold no record, and the mechanism is a classification decision that put internet suspension outside the national crime-records apparatus with no proposal to bring it in. Subtraction across a set of incommensurable counts and a non-existent one is not available in any form.
notes: Neither side is a series and the pair is carried because each is misread alone. The UT's 93 shown by itself reads as a parliamentary finding, which it is not - the Committee asked and the scrutinised party wrote back a number that nobody verified, sampled or reconciled, and the report's formatting makes that easy to miss. The absence shown by itself reads as a data gap, when the Union's own answer to the counting question was to point Parliament at the UT's website rather than to say whether it holds the number: it declined to occupy either position. The Committee's own conclusion is the connective tissue - that there is no mechanism to verify any count, because the only shutdown figures anywhere in its report are self-reported by the bodies doing the shutting down.

title: Four official turnout values for one election, and the report that would settle them

a.label: What the Election Commission has published the turnout to be

b.label: The statistical report that would fix the basis - not published, for J&K or for any state polled in 2024

framing: The Commission published four values for one 2024 turnout quantity and disclosed in its own chart footnote that its comparison changes basis at the final point, and the document that would settle which value is which does not exist for any state polled that year.
gapReason: The differences between the four values are not a gap but four different definitions of one quantity, and two of the five constituency figures move down rather than up between documents, so they cannot even be ordered as provisional and final. On the other side there is no figure at all to subtract towards: the statistical report is missing, so the postal-inclusive turnout on which the 2014 comparison stands cannot be computed for 2024 from anything published. A difference between a set of incompatible bases and a non-existent document is not a quantity.
notes: Shown alone, the four values look like ordinary revision and the absence looks like a delay. Together they are the finding: the basis is unstable and the instrument that would stabilise it is missing for a whole cohort of elections. The absence must not be presented as J&K-specific - it applies to all eight state assemblies polled in 2024 - and the four-value divergence must not be presented as error, since each value is correct on its own basis and the Commission discloses the change in a footnote to the chart that carries it.

title: Turnout, against the thing it is used as a proxy for

a.label: Votes cast as a share of registered electors

b.label: Acceptance of the constitutional arrangement - no agreed definition exists

framing: Every argument about what the 2024 turnout means is an argument about a quantity with no definition, and turnout is pressed into service as its proxy precisely because the thing itself cannot be measured.
gapReason: There is nothing on the second side to subtract. Turnout is a ratio of votes to electors and acceptance of a constitutional arrangement is not a quantity at all: no agreed definition of it exists, so it could not be collected even in principle, and no arithmetic connects a participation rate to a proposition about legitimacy. The two are placed together so that a turnout figure is not read as an answer to a question it does not address.
notes: The pair is carried because the turnout figure is unusually easy to over-read in both directions. A 63.88 per cent assembly turnout is above the 2024 parliamentary figure in the same territory and below the 2014 assembly figure recomputed on the same territory, so it supports a rise and a fall depending on the comparator chosen; and its divisional split of 55.50 per cent in Kashmir against 73.15 per cent in Jammu, with Srinagar-city constituencies as low as 19.81 per cent, is not visible in the headline at all. None of that bears on the second side, which remains undefined.

title: Domicile certificates issued, against the sub-count the Union would not publish

a.label: Certificates issued, as the Union published them

b.label: Certificates to persons who were not previously permanent residents - unpublished by the Union, and produced within months once an Assembly asked

framing: The Union published 3.2 million certificates and, once, the 3.1 million of them that went to people who already held or depended on permanent-resident status, and never published the complement that the whole argument is about.
gapReason: The residual is a real subtraction and is not the missing quantity. Taking 3,108,682 from 3,231,353 leaves 122,671, but that is a mixture the reply gives no way to decompose: it necessarily contains persons on the migrant limb, children of central-government officials, children of qualifying parents, and persons entitled to a permanent-resident certificate who never held one in their own name, because the published denominator is certificate-holding rather than entitlement. Presenting it as a count of newcomers would be exactly the laundering this instrument exists to prevent. The one figure that addresses the second side, 83,742, is on a different period under a different category name and cannot be netted against anything here.
notes: The order of the two sides is the argument, and it cuts for the government on one half: 3.1 million of 3.2 million certificates converted an existing status, which is a conversion rather than an influx and is the strongest single fact the case for has. What the pair adds is that the Union published that half and not the other, for five and a half years, while its own answers show the split was separable from the start - and that the complement appeared within months of a legislature existing to ask for it. That is what makes this a not-published rather than a not-collected.

title: Four units for one land count, and the year-wise series with a stated unit that nobody publishes

a.label: What the Union and the Assembly have said the non-resident land count is

b.label: Year-wise, district-wise transfers with the unit stated - not published by the Union, which stopped in 2023

framing: Five official answers give the same quantity in four units and two irreconcilable levels, and the Union's own series ends in 2023 while the count itself continues in a legislature the Union says holds the subject.
gapReason: There is nothing to subtract. Properties, plots, persons and area are four different objects, one answer states no period at all, and two official figures - two persons since August 2019 against 57 persons in calendar 2021 alone - cannot both describe the same object without an explanation no document gives. On the other side there is no published Union series at all after 2022. And the relayed year breakdown that would close the 2019 stub and 2023 does not reconcile, giving 512 against a stated 631 with no outlet printing 2023, so the residual must not be reconstructed by subtraction.
notes: Both sides are misread alone. The counts shown alone read as a trend, when the unit changes under them and the Union's own two answers disagree by an order of magnitude about the same window. The absence shown alone reads as concealment, when the more precise finding is a termination: the Union answered whenever asked until April 2023 and then published nothing, while the J&K Revenue Department went on holding district, area and value detail and produced all three when a restored Assembly asked. And the whole count sits under a definitional caution neither side can ignore, since after 31 October 2019 a buyer from Kargil is a person from outside the territory by construction.

title: Seats counted empty, against the causes the statute requires and nobody publishes

a.label: Panchayat and sarpanch seats recorded vacant

b.label: The cause recorded against each - statutorily required to exist before the seat can be filled, and published for one cause only

framing: The administration counts the empty seats to the unit and publishes the cause of exactly one of them, leaving 725 seats emptied by death, resignation and 'etc' in its own words - in a system where the statute makes the cause a condition of filling the seat.
gapReason: The residual is a real subtraction and is not a breakdown. Of the 1,032-seat increase between the two points, 307 are attributed to the election of Block Development Council chairpersons, leaving 725 unattributed - but that residual mixes death, resignation, disqualification and whatever the authority's 'etc' covers, and nothing in the published record decomposes it. A single number standing for four causes is not a cause series, and no arithmetic can separate them.
notes: The order of the sides is the argument, and the second side is unusually well grounded: section 8(1) of the Panchayati Raj Act makes the cause of a vacancy and its duration a statutory element, so the determination must be made before a by-election can be called, and the department annexed halqa-wise lists of vacant seats to its own orders. The only disaggregation that exists anywhere is a spoken remark at a 2019 press conference giving around five resignations and around 33 deaths, set against departmental accounts of hundreds of resignations announced in newspaper advertisements of which fifty were formally accepted. A vacancy series that cannot distinguish a seat nobody stood for from a seat whose holder was killed is not a vacancy series.

title: Complaints the national Commission registers from J&K, against the share it may not investigate

a.label: Cases from J&K registered with the National Human Rights Commission

b.label: The share of them naming the Army or a central armed police force - the Commission may only seek a report, and has never published the number

framing: Registrations from the territory have risen fivefold since the State Commission was abolished, and nobody publishes what fraction of them concern respondents the national Commission is barred by statute from investigating.
gapReason: There is nothing to subtract. The first side is a count of cases and the second is a share of that same count which has never been published in any form, so no residual exists to compute. The one column in the instrument that looks as though it might supply it does not: the Defence and Para-Military custodial column reads zero for J&K in every year, but it records intimations received under a duty addressed to District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police that does not run to the armed forces at all - so its zero is a property of the reporting duty and must never be substituted for the missing share.
notes: The order of the sides is the argument, and it is the whole of the substitution question. The rise from 194 to 995 is the strongest single fact the case for has, and it is not disputed. What it cannot establish on its own is whether the body receiving those cases can do anything about the respondents they name, because section 19 confines the Commission in respect of the armed forces to seeking a report from the Central Government and then dropping the matter or recommending. The missing number is producible by the holder and by nobody else, since the Commission assigns an incident code to every case and records the state of origin of every case and prints both facts separately in the same document.

title: Cases the national Commission used to hand to a state body, against the caseload nobody inherited

a.label: J&K cases transferred to a State Human Rights Commission

b.label: What became of the cases pending before the abolished commissions - the winding-up orders do not use the word

framing: The national Commission's own disposal table records the abolition as a column that runs 38, 51, 10 and then zero forever, and the orders that caused it dispose of vehicles and furniture by name and say nothing about a pending case.
gapReason: The two sides are not the same population and neither is a residual of the other. The first counts cases the national Commission sent to a state body in a given year; the second is the stock of matters already before the state bodies when they were abolished, for which no figure has ever been published - and for the information commission the last published pendency figure is five years stale at abolition, so it cannot even be used as a proxy. Subtraction would imply a subset relation that no instrument asserts.
notes: Each side is misread alone. The zero column looks like a fall in referrals and is a structural consequence of there being no counterparty, unfootnoted in every volume that prints it. The absence looks like a records-management problem and is measurable at both ends for at least one of the seven commissions: the Central Information Commission's own published index shows no decision against any J&K public authority until 15 May 2020, 197 days after the state forum ceased. That is a rare instance in this phase of an absence with hard edges on both sides, and both edges come from the successor body's own index.

title: Finance Commission grants allocated to J&K's panchayats, against grants released

a.label: Allocated to Gram Panchayats under the XIV Finance Commission award

b.label: Actually released

framing: Both sides come from one table in one written answer, in one unit, on one recipient - so the gap is a real subtraction rather than a comparison, and it runs from 6 crore rupees in the first year to the whole 1,049.49 crore of the last.
notes: THE ONLY PAIR IN THIS DROP WHOSE GAP IS COMPUTABLE, and it is worth saying why the other thirteen are not: everywhere else in this phase the two sides are on different units, different populations, different dates or different instruments, or one side does not exist at all. Here they are two columns of one annexure, printed side by side by the holder, in rupees crore, for the same recipient and the same years. The subtraction gives 6.24, 111.32, 204.18, 234.57 and 1,049.49 crore rupees year by year, and 1,605.80 over the award - and that total, together with the 53.64 per cent release rate, is DERIVED here and is stated nowhere in the answer. Read the gap with two cautions. It is not new: an earlier award records 81 per cent of an earmark unsecured for non-fulfilment of prescribed conditions, so shortfall against allocation has a precedent with a stated cause. And the final year carries two facts at once - the referent changed on 31 October 2019, seven months in, and the release was zero - which nothing retrieved connects, so the pair must not be read as showing that the reorganisation stopped the money.

title: Forty-one per cent of what

a.label: The share of the divisible pool the Finance Commission recommended and the Union accepted

b.label: The share of the Union's whole tax take that actually moved to the states

framing: The 41 per cent and the 32 per cent are the same policy measured against two bases, and the distance between them is the divisible pool — which is why neither number answers the question the other is usually quoted for.
gapReason: Different denominators. The two are reconciled not by subtraction but by a third series, divisible-pool-share-gtr: 41 per cent of a pool that is 79.9 per cent of gross tax revenue is 32.8 per cent of gross tax revenue. Subtracting one from the other produces a number that measures nothing.
notes: The commonest error in this whole subject is reading either of these as the other. A reader told the states' share rose from 32 to 42 per cent and a reader told the states receive about a third of central taxes are being given the same fact on two bases, and each will draw the opposite conclusion from the one the pair supports.

title: Did the money the Union does not share double

a.label: Cesses and surcharges including the GST Compensation Cess: 10.4 to 19.9 per cent of gross tax revenue

b.label: The same levies excluding the GST Compensation Cess, which is earmarked to the states: 10.4 to 15.3 per cent

framing: Whether the Union's non-shareable revenue doubled over the decade depends entirely on whether a cess collected by the Union and earmarked to the states counts as revenue the Union keeps.
gapReason: These are not two measures of a quantity with a gap between them; they are the same collections summed on two definitions, and the choice of definition inverts the sign of the FY2017-18 movement. Subtracting them yields the compensation cess, which is a third thing again.
notes: Neither side may be shown alone. On the inclusive convention the share rises 1.91-fold and rises in FY2017-18; on the exclusive convention it rises 1.47-fold and falls in FY2017-18. Both are honest sums of the same published line items, and the whole of the difference is definitional — there is no evidentiary disagreement anywhere in the spread.

title: The final number and the missing certificate

a.label: The certified divisible pool as relayed by the paying party, six years

b.label: The Article 279(1) certificate itself, which has never been published for any year

framing: The number the Constitution declares final is in the public record for six years out of seventy-six, and the document that makes it final is in the public record for none.
gapReason: One side is a figure and the other is the absence of the instrument behind it. There is no subtraction between a number and the document that would authenticate it.
notes: This is the pair that governs how every fiscal series in this drop should be read. The divisible pool is the denominator of the entire Centre-state fiscal argument, and for ten of the sixteen years carried here it has no certified basis at all.

title: The published zero and the unpublished order

a.label: MGNREGA money released to West Bengal, ending at a published 0.00

b.label: The section 27 order that produced the zero, which has never been published

framing: The Union publishes the consequence of exercising a statutory power against one state for fifty-one months and does not publish the exercise, so the only instrument that records the decision is a description of it in Parliament.
gapReason: A rupee figure and an unpublished administrative order are not two measures of one quantity. What the pair records is that the effect is measurable and the decision is not.
notes: Read with bihar-mgnrega-funds-released, which runs through the same three years on the same table with no stoppage. Without the Bihar row the zero looks like an outcome; with it, the zero is legible as an act.

title: The states' fifty per cent and the Union's forty-nine

a.label: What the Union's own accounts show going out, against gross tax revenue

b.label: The states' demand for 50 per cent of the divisible pool, and the Union's reply that they already receive more than 49 per cent of gross revenue receipts

framing: Eighteen of twenty-eight states asked the Sixteenth Finance Commission for half the divisible pool and the Union replied that they already receive nearly half of everything it takes in, and both statements are true because the two denominators are different.
gapReason: A demand is not a measurement, and the two figures are computed on different bases — one on the divisible pool, the other on gross revenue receipts including non-tax revenue and grants. The Union's components for its own figure are not published, so no bridge can be built between them here.
notes: The states' 50 per cent is a count of pleadings the Commission published, not a measurement, and must render labelled as advocacy. The Union's more-than-49 is a measurement on a denominator it chose and whose components it does not publish. Neither may be shown as the answer to the other.

title: Collected against credited

a.label: The compensation cess as the Union's receipt head records it

b.label: What the auditor finds reached the funds the cesses were levied for

framing: A cess sits outside the divisible pool because it is levied for a stated purpose, and the only instrument that reports whether the purpose received the money is an audit report neither government publishes.
gapReason: Collections under a receipt head and credits to a reserve fund in the Public Account are different accounting events on different funds, so the difference between them is not a shortfall in any single ledger. The auditor computes it precisely because neither account computes it on itself.
notes: This is the strongest disciplining instrument in the phase and the pair exists to show why: the input is one party's records, the comparator is another set of records, the operation is the auditor's, and the output appears in neither party's account of itself. On the GST Compensation Cess it produced an admission in February 2020 and a correction in FY2019-20.

title: Thirty thousand crore outside the budget, and no national table of it

a.label: Union money reaching Tamil Nadu's implementing agencies without entering the State Budget

b.label: Whether the Union publishes this channel by state anywhere at all

framing: The Union holds this quantity by state and by scheme in its own payment system, discloses it to a state's auditor and to whoever asks the right parliamentary question, and publishes no national table of it.
gapReason: One side is one state's figure over nine years and the other is the question whether the corresponding national figure is published anywhere. There is no subtraction between a measurement and an unanswered question about its publication.
notes: The finding this pair carries is that the only routine publication of the quantity is thirty-odd separate state audit reports, on different templates in different years — and that this drop did not sweep the Union side exhaustively, so the absence is declared narrowly and must not be read as closed.

title: Devolution as the Union accounts for it, against devolution as the states account for receiving it

a.label: Devolution as the Union and its Commission account for paying it

b.label: Devolution as the twenty-eight states account for receiving it, compiled on one basis from audited state accounts

framing: Every figure in this phase's fiscal spine is a Union-origin figure, and the counterpart the instrument would need — the states' own audited receipts on one common basis — is not built anywhere this drop could reach.
gapReason: Side b is not authored: no compiled state-side series exists in this drop. The pair is recorded as owed rather than left silently absent, because the judgement that these two things belong side by side has been made and only one side can be filled.
notes: The trap this pair exists to mark: a source that looks independent but is produced by a party to the dispute is not a check. State figures on Centre-state transfers are not independent of the states and Union figures are not independent of the Centre. The Reserve Bank's State Finances: A Study of Budgets looks like the missing counterpart and is not one — it is compiled from the states' own budget documents, so it is a common BASIS rather than independent EVIDENCE, and it cannot audit what the Union actually released. That characterisation was established in this run from the publication's own explanatory note, but the exact publication URL was not carried into the research parts, so no finding in this drop rests on it and side b stays unauthored. What can be built from retrieved material is the audited state-accounts route: the Sixteenth Finance Commission sources its own state-finance chapter to States' Finance Accounts, which is the CAG-compiled base rather than budget documents, and the state audit reports carry the per-state figures. Filling side b means compiling that, state by state, on one edition and one definition.

title: Collected for the Fund, and what the Fund got

a.label: What the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess raised, being revenue the states have no claim on

b.label: What reached the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Fund, being the purpose that justifies the exclusion

framing: A cess sits outside the divisible pool because it is levied for a named purpose, and this is the one case in the drop where the Union publishes the levy and the purpose in adjacent columns of one row, so the two can be read against each other without an auditor in between.
notes: Subtraction is available here, unusually, because the Union performs it itself: the answer prints a Balance column equal to (A) minus (B), and it is that column which fixes the first two years at zero rather than blank. Two cautions on what the gap means. Year by year it resets, so from FY2023-24 it reads as over-transfer; cumulatively across the five published years collections are 387,226.31 crore against transfers of 377,213.61, so the Fund is still 10,012.70 crore behind. And side b mixes transfer into the Fund with utilisation out of it in one column, so a large figure cannot be decomposed. Read against PR-53, which is the same question about the GST Compensation Cess and where the comparator is an auditor's rather than the publisher's own.

title: Allocated to West Bengal, and released to West Bengal

a.label: The central allocation the Union approved for West Bengal under Samagra Shiksha, which continued through both nil years and rose in the second

b.label: The central share actually released, which went to nil and stayed there

framing: An allocation and a release are two separate decisions by the same Ministry about the same money in the same year, and this is the state where they came apart completely while the allocation carried on rising.
notes: The gap is 3,744.19 crore across the two nil years alone and is computable because both columns are the Union's own, in one table, for one state, in one unit. What makes it legible is the two controls beside it on the same table. Bihar was released between 70.8 and 93.8 per cent of allocation in every year including the years West Bengal received nothing, so a shortfall is the ordinary condition of this scheme and a zero is not the extreme of that continuum. And Tamil Nadu's zero carries the Union's own footnote recording 362.81 crore paid in arrears the following year, where West Bengal's carries none — which is the difference between a delay and a stoppage, visible only because the table runs five years.

title: The number that was asked for and the number that was given

a.label: Tamil Nadu's inter-se share of the states' portion of the divisible pool — the figure the Government supplies when asked what a state gets back per rupee it contributes

b.label: The ratio actually asked for, which no instrument in the country computes because one of its inputs is declared not to exist

framing: Asked in the Rajya Sabha whether Tamil Nadu receives less than 29 paise in the rupee and for tax devolution per one rupee state-wise, the Government answered with 4.079 per cent — a share of a pool, not a return per rupee contributed — and did not say it was answering a different question.
gapReason: One side is a published percentage of one base and the other is a quantity nobody computes; there is no subtraction between a number and a question. The two are not even in the same units — an inter-se share is a state's slice of what all states receive, and the ratio asked for is a state's receipt divided by its own contribution, whose denominator has three components of which one is stated by its holder not to be maintained.
notes: This pair exists to name a move the four-value absence vocabulary cannot express. The Government has not refused this figure — there is no refusal anywhere in more than ten dated requests across twenty-five years — and it has not said the figure does not exist. It has, four separate times, supplied an adjacent published number in its place without saying it had substituted. Substitution is neither withholding nor non-collection, and it leaves a reader who was answered believing they were answered. Side a is a real, correct, carefully sourced series, and putting it here is not a criticism of it: the point is precisely that the substitute is a good number for a different question.

title: India's imports from China: the two countries' own figures, same year, same commodity basis

a.label: India reports (CIF)

b.label: China reports (FOB)

framing: Both governments publish this flow and they do not agree. India reports US$126.963bn for calendar 2024; China reports US$120.463bn. Neither is the corrective and neither may be shown alone, because a reader given one figure would take it for the figure.
gapReason: The DIFFERENCE is arithmetic — US$6.500bn in 2024, 5.40 per cent of the Chinese figure — but it is not a gap, and the schema is right to refuse the word for a contested pair. A gap is a shortfall of one quantity against another that bounds it; this is the size of a disagreement between two authorities measuring the same flow, and neither bounds the other. The magnitude is stated because it is evidence about the CAUSE: an importer-minus-exporter excess of that order is consistent with the CIF/FOB valuation convention, which is what makes the 20.80 per cent excess on the opposite flow (PR-60) the anomaly rather than this one. Subtracting it would produce a third number no one publishes.

title: India's exports to China: the direction where the divergence is too large to be freight

a.label: India reports (FOB)

b.label: China reports (CIF)

framing: China records more Indian goods arriving than India records leaving — US$17.999bn against US$14.899bn in calendar 2024. The importer's figure exceeding the exporter's is the expected direction, but the size is not: 20.80 per cent where the mirror flow shows 5.40. The pair exists because the anomaly is only visible when both sides are held together; either series alone reads as an ordinary export series.
gapReason: The difference is US$3.099bn in 2024, 20.80 per cent of India's figure, and it is a disagreement rather than a gap for the same reason as PR-59: neither side bounds the other. The magnitude is the whole point of the pair — it is four times the excess on the mirror flow and beyond what freight and insurance explain. The leading candidate is entrepot attribution through Hong Kong, sized in P-119 as large enough to contain it and NOT established as its cause.
